note: Preseason: 2026 league not yet renewed, so this is a stash watchlist against 2025 end-of-season rosters, not a live bid sheet. FAAB resets to 100 dollars at the draft. Migrated to the 3-layer valuation model (asset → worth → edge → verdict + rec-confidence); rate_basis is projection-only until games generate a recent snap/route trend. A live in-season run reads rate off the last 3-4 weeks.

targets.why: Named Miami's presumptive starter (3yr/$67.5M, Tua to ATL). Rushing profile = konami premium in this format.
targets.asset: Konami rushing-QB floor as Miami's named starter — rush yds (1/10) + 6-pt rush TDs out-floor the pocket streamers this league leaves free.
targets.my_team_impact: Your 2025 QB room was Lawrence + Nix — streamer-band pocket passers. A named-starter rushing QB out-floors both in this scoring; he's the cheap route to the QB edge you've never paid for.
targets.worth: a rd10+ draft flier / minimal FAAB
targets.confidence_why: named starter, but the rushing volume is a projection — no in-season trend yet to confirm the role
targets.competition: QB-punt league — only mfkr and DiaperDutyDaddy pay up at QB, and they chase elites, not battle-winners

targets.why: Recovery encouraging after missing 2025; could take Chuba Hubbard's lead role in-season.
targets.asset: Lead-back lottery ticket — a Hubbard takeover is standalone RB2/FLEX volume, the scarcest resource in a 2-RB/2-FLEX league.
targets.my_team_impact: With 2 RB + 2 FLEX and only 5 bench, a lead-back lottery ticket beats your RB4/5 tier (Rodriguez/Gainwell class) outright — and stashing now buys out the 60-dollar-plus frenzy his promotion would trigger.
targets.worth: a late-round stash now; 60+ FAAB the week a takeover actually lands
targets.confidence_why: the value is contingent on a takeover that hasn't happened — a speculative stash, not a locked role
targets.competition: ENOTS systematically overbids RB opportunity (price-to-beat 27, n=73); StoneBone69 files claims on everything — median bid just 2, but 23 fully clears him

targets.why: RB2-role buzz after a strong offseason; cheap RB volume matters in a 2-FLEX league.
targets.asset: Rotational DAL RB2 — cheap committee volume, but no standalone starter/FLEX value as things stand.
targets.my_team_impact: A rotational DAL RB2 doesn't crack your starters or FLEX — last-bench-spot churn material only. Fine as a final-round dart, not worth displacing a lottery ticket with a clearer path.
targets.confidence_why: committee role, buzz-based and unproven — nothing to bid up on yet
targets.competition: Sladsous owns Javonte Williams (DAL) but is the league's most rookie-averse drafter — low

targets.why: Biggest TE ADP riser two months running, elite 2025 efficiency (97th pct YPRR) — but QB downgrade to Willis tempers it.
targets.asset: Post-hype TE with elite 2025 efficiency (97th pct YPRR), capped by the Willis QB downgrade and an unsettled role.
targets.my_team_impact: You held Kittle in 2025 and hunt elite TEs; a TE2 stash is a dead spot on a 5-man bench. Only relevant if you miss the elite-TE window at the draft — then he's the stream-first candidate, not a roster hold.
targets.worth: watchlist only — a stream-first name if you miss the elite-TE window
targets.confidence_why: efficiency is real but role + QB are unsettled, and a TE2 is a dead bench spot for your build
targets.competition: bwalsh89 (TE rounds 2-5 in 4 of 6 drafts) and newly TE-aggressive Stipe are the market for post-hype TEs

targets.why: Trending on name recognition after a 1yr/$2.35M prove-it re-signing.
targets.asset: Depth WR behind McLaurin — the exact archetype this league replaces for free in-season.
targets.my_team_impact: Depth WR behind McLaurin is exactly the archetype this league replaces for free in-season, and your WR room (JSN, A.J. Brown, Evans, Pearsall in 2025) has no slot he threatens. Trending list noise — skip.
targets.worth: 0 FAAB — no slot he threatens on your roster
targets.confidence_why: clear no-fit on a deep WR room — high confidence in the pass
